quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on team communication and late-game execution
quotes.excerpt: our communication down the stretch, just being able to handle situations differently.
quotes.quote: Our communication down the stretch, just being able to handle situations differently. But again, we talk about the two minutes of the game, or the last four actually, just being able to have a plan, make sure we got that down pat, understanding how we want to guard and cover things and then knowing what we can go to down the stretch. So it was a great communication, great film session with these guys to be able to see exactly what we are capable of doing and what we need to execute down the stretch.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the Pelicans focused on late game communication and execution in film sessions to better handle situational basketball down the stretch.

structured.context: Head coach Jamahl Mosley discusses the importance of team communication and execution during the final minutes of games.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on managing Jeremiah's aggression and foul trouble
quotes.excerpt: I'd rather have to say whoa than sic 'em.
quotes.quote: It's tricky with young guys because I'd rather have to say whoa than sic 'em. And that's the thing with him, we can taper that back a little bit. I don't have to get him going, but just understanding when and where. And the last one he got, he wasn't trying to foul, but the other two, I think it's part of aggression, knowing when and where and what you're able to get away with.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on managing young player aggression and foul trouble: I would rather have to say whoa than sic em.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses managing the aggression and foul trouble of a young player named Jeremiah.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the Pelicans' offensive identity and paint scoring
quotes.excerpt: we have a team that gets downhill very well. They touch the paint.
quotes.quote: With the team that we have, and adding a Benedict to the group, we have a team that gets downhill very well. They touch the paint, and that's what we've honed in on, and the ability to get to the free throw line, the ability to attack the basket. And now with that power that we have to get to the rim, being able to find open shooters and being able to trust the pass. So that ball's got to move once it does touch the paint.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the Pelicans offensive identity is built on getting downhill and touching the paint, noting that the ball has to move once they get inside.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the offensive identity of the Pelicans following the addition of Benedict to the roster.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Zion's defensive impact and system trust
quotes.excerpt: the team's best defenders are guarding him. And so now taking that challenge on the other way.
quotes.quote: Just trusting our system, knowing he's so gifted, so talented, so strong in what he's able to do offensively, and just transfer that to the defensive end of the floor. Take on all challenges because the team's best defenders are guarding him. And so now taking that challenge on the other way, can you guard the team's best guy as well? And I think that's what great players want to do, and they're willing to do that, and that makes the team that much better when your best player is willing to step in to guard the other team's best player.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley is challenging Zion to take on the defensive assignment of guarding the other team best player, saying that is what great players want to do.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley challenges Zion Williamson to translate his offensive talent to the defensive end of the floor.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the Utah Jazz's size and length
quotes.excerpt: these guys have a lot of length and size on the floor that they can throw out there.
quotes.quote: I talked to Will about it this summer. I mean, their starting five can go Hayes, when Nerk is healthy you got Nerk, you got Triple J, you got Lauri, you got Bailey. These guys have a lot of length and size on the floor that they can throw out there at any given time, and Will's not afraid to play it. And I think that's extremely unique to get these guys to be able to buy into that, and the disruption that they cause on the offensive end for us.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley praises the Utah Jazz for their unique size and length, noting that Will Hardy is not afraid to utilize his big lineups to cause disruption.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses the size and length of the Utah Jazz roster and his conversation with coach Will Hardy.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on improving ball movement and reducing turnovers
quotes.excerpt: we had those stall out moments, but what one thing that was glaring was some of the turnovers.
quotes.quote: We had those stall out moments, but what one thing that was glaring was some of the turnovers, the intention was right. We had two passes to Eve in the middle of the lane that, how do we connect those? We had a couple situations where we got the stop, got on the break, and we don't finish it because we mishap a lob. And so I think those situations are ones that we can celebrate because we're trying with the intention to make the right play. Now we've just got to break it down on film, walk through it in practice and understand exactly, the intent is right, now how do we connect those dots?
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the Pelicans are working on connecting the dots after turnover issues, noting that while the intention behind the passes is right, the execution needs to improve.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley addresses the need to improve ball movement and reduce turnovers after reviewing game film.
